correctness.rationale: Computing ΔG_s=s^-4(r²-ds²)G_s reduces every zero to d<y<dv, y=r²/a², v=(b/a)². Zero equation Q(y)=(1-w)/w has Q=v^((d+4)/2)(y-d)/(dv-y) exp(-(v-1)y/(2v)). Its exact log derivative (v-1)(h²-C)/(2v(D²-h²)), h=y-d(1+v)/2, D=d(v-1)/2, C=d²(v-1)²/4-2dv, has zero, two turning points, or cusp according to C<0,>0,=0; therefore at most three roots with stated simple/double/triple boundaries and weight interval. Independent algebra checks at d=2 give v_c=3+2√2 and γ_d=C'(v_c)=4√2; b/a=3,w=.1 has w_-≈0.051745899709,w_+≈0.200018095698, hence 3 simple shells. Integrating Q'/Q over the interval of width 2√C yields the sharp (v-v_c)^(3/2) weight cusp and √ separation. Positive definite Fourier transform follows as positive Gaussian mixture; strict radial monotonicity follows from negative radial derivative. These analytic arguments cover all dimensions and weights, unlike numerical witnesses.
